PullRequest.Title: notifications: attribute extension messages to audited types
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Notification telemetry currently identifies an originating extension but cannot distinguish individual messages or progress operations. This prevents understanding which notifications new Agents-window users see, dismiss, act on, or cancel.

- Add the `notificationTelemetry` proposed API with optional `notificationId` on `MessageOptions` and `ProgressOptions`, and forward it through the extension-host bridges.
- Accept only audited semantic IDs scoped to the originating extension and message/progress kind. Unsupported or foreign IDs retain generic attribution; arbitrary producer strings and notification content are never collected.
- Tag 21 built-in notification types: nine GitHub Authentication types, eight Git types, and four TypeScript types.
- Preserve existing notification behavior, button results, deduplication rules, telemetry consent, and event schemas. Add proposal-gating, privacy, bridge round-trip, and correlation tests.

## Validation

Passed on a branch based on `origin/main`:

- The following targeted test command: **55 tests passed**.

  ```powershell
  .\scripts\test.bat --reporter dot `
    --run src\vs\workbench\test\common\notificationTelemetry.test.ts `
    --run src\vs\workbench\api\test\browser\extHostMessagerService.test.ts `
    --run src\vs\workbench\api\test\browser\mainThreadProgress.test.ts `
    --run src\vs\workbench\test\common\notifications.test.ts `
    --run src\vs\workbench\services\progress\test\browser\progressService.test.ts
  ```

- `.\node_modules\.bin\tsc.cmd --project extensions\github-authentication\tsconfig.json --noEmit`: **passed**.
- `.\node_modules\.bin\tsc.cmd --project extensions\git\tsconfig.json --noEmit`: **passed**.
- `.\node_modules\.bin\tsc.cmd --project extensions\typescript-language-features\tsconfig.json --noEmit`: **passed**.
- `npm run vscode-dts-compile-check`: **passed**.
- `npm run eslint -- $files`, with `$files` containing the 24 changed TypeScript/declaration targets: **passed**.
- `git diff --check`: **passed**.

Earlier focused checks also verified all 21 producer IDs against the registry, generated proposal registration, and the extracted notification telemetry schemas and measurement classifications.

`npm run compile-client`: **blocked during gulp initialization** because the checkout declares Copilot runtime `1.0.103` while the installed `@github/copilot-sdk` bundles `1.0.102`. Fresh client JavaScript for the targeted tests was prepared with the repository's standalone transpiler; the runtime guard was not disabled. The earlier client-wide type-check also failed on dependency/SDK incompatibilities. Full integration/smoke tests and live provider flows were not run.

## Reviewer and rollout notes

- Historical generic events cannot be retroactively classified.
- Third-party extensions such as vscode-icons and Java still need producer adoption and audited allowlist entries. Generic agent-host progress and Copilot Chat coverage are unchanged.
- Products with explicit proposal allowlists for these built-in extensions must also authorize `notificationTelemetry`; product allowlists override extension manifests.
- Button positions remain positional telemetry, not inferred action semantics or success outcomes. Modal dialogs remain outside notification exposure/interaction telemetry.
- No linked issue; this follows up on the new-user Agents-window notification analysis.

Scenarios.Scenario: Extension message API calls, including the newly tagged Git, GitHub Authentication, and TypeScript prompts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The extension host validates the proposal only when notificationId is supplied, sends the existing show-message RPC, and the main thread creates the existing notification. The diff adds one constant string to that RPC and one bounded allowlist lookup before notification creation. Existing exposure/interaction telemetry occurs only after rendering or user action and is not a new prerequisite for showing the notification.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Extension-host $showMessage RPC with an optional constant notificationId field
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one existing RPC per extension message; no extra RPC is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same RPC carried severity, message, source, options, and actions without notificationId.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The RPC already had to complete to create the notification. The added bounded string payload does not add another round trip.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing notificationShown and notificationInteraction telemetry submission through publicLog2
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per logical notification/surface plus existing user interactions; the diff changes only the bounded notificationId value, not event count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same telemetry events were emitted with generic extension.message attribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Exposure telemetry occurs after the notification is visible, and interaction telemetry after an action; neither is added to notification creation's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Git missing-repository detection stats each workspace folder's .git path before deciding whether to show the existing warning
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One asynchronous stat per workspace folder, grouped in the existing Promise.all; unchanged by notification metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical per-workspace-folder stats preceded the same warning.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This pre-existing check determines whether the warning is needed; the diff neither adds nor moves it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One lookup per shown extension message. The effective allowlist cardinality is one map entry for extension/kind and at most eight IDs in its array; producer IDs in this PR are constants. Git repository-limit messages can occur per opened repository, but the new work remains one bounded lookup per already-existing notification.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Message RPCs retain their existing concurrency and UI notification scheduling. The diff adds no queue, fan-out, parallel task, or new RPC; each existing show-message request carries one additional field.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The allowlist is a process-static map and needs no warm-up or invalidation. There is no result cache, but each lookup is bounded to at most eight comparisons, and misses are not retried inside the bridge.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the full extension-host-to-main-thread call path shows no added message, telemetry event, filesystem operation, or loop; only an extra DTO field and bounded lookup were added.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact notification frequency varies by workspace and producer, but changed work is a short constant identifier, one small proposal-array check, and a lookup over no more than eight entries per already-existing message.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. CPU, allocation, IPC bytes, and telemetry cardinality remain bounded and negligible relative to the existing notification RPC and rendering.

Scenarios.Scenario: GitHub browser and device-code sign-in progress notifications
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The extension starts the existing progress RPC without awaiting it and immediately runs the OAuth task. The diff adds notificationId only to the start-progress DTO; it is checked and allowlisted once when progress starts, not on throttled progress reports or device-code polling. OAuth completion remains gated by browser callback/token exchange or device-code polling, not telemetry attribution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing $startProgress RPC from extension host to main thread, now carrying one semantic ID
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One start RPC per sign-in progress operation; progress reports and end RPC cardinality are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same start RPC created the same progress UI with generic extension.progress attribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The start RPC is fire-and-catch and the OAuth task begins immediately; the extra field does not add a round trip or serialize polling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Browser OAuth token exchange or repeated device-code access-token POSTs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Browser flow performs the existing token exchange once; device-code flow performs at most 120/json.interval existing polling requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical browser opening, callback waiting, token exchange, and polling occurred under the same progress operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These requests determine authentication completion. notificationId is processed once at progress start and is not consulted in the network loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing env.openExternal/command bridge calls used by the sign-in flow
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One browser-open operation and bounded command calls per flow, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same external-browser and command operations were performed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Opening the browser is required for authentication; the diff does not add or move it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing once-per-surface exposure and interaction events; semantic attribution does not create additional events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The events used generic extension.progress attribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the OAuth completion critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One metadata lookup per sign-in flow. Device-code network polling remains up to 120/json.interval attempts over two minutes, but the diff does not run metadata work per attempt. Progress reports remain throttled at 100 ms by existing code.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each user-initiated sign-in flow has one start RPC, existing report RPCs, and one end RPC. The diff adds no parallel OAuth requests, polling attempts, or progress operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache participates in OAuth progress attribution. The static allowlist lookup behaves identically on cold and warm calls; OAuth token/network state is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the progress bridge, 100 ms report throttle, main-thread start handler, and OAuth loops establish exact placement and multiplicity.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: OAuth request latency and concurrent sign-ins vary, but the changed mechanism is provably once per progress start rather than per poll or per report.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff does not amplify network polling, IPC report frequency, or progress rendering.

Scenarios.Scenario: TypeScript server startup with an invalid configured server path
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing synchronous existsSync validates the selected tsserver path; on failure the existing warning is sent, the version resets, and the existing child process is spawned with the fallback path. The diff adds only constant notification metadata to the warning RPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous existence check for the configured tsserver path
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing check per server process creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical existsSync check selected the fallback before the same warning.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already on the server startup critical path; the metadata change neither adds nor relocates it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn or fork the selected TypeScript server process
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing child process per TS server role/start; unchanged by the warning metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fallback path was spawned after invalid-path detection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for language-service startup; no new process or delay is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing extension show-warning RPC carrying the new constant ID
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one existing warning RPC for each failed path validation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same unawaited warning RPC was sent without the semantic field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The warning call remains unawaited and does not delay fallback process spawning.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One path check and at most one warning per TS server process creation; server count and restart behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing TS server process creation semantics are unchanged. No additional subprocess, filesystem check, or concurrent task is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Version selection/reset behavior is unchanged. Attribution uses the same static allowlist on every warning; there is no new cache state or miss retry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: adjacent code directly shows the synchronous path check, unawaited warning, reset, and spawn ordering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: TS server restart frequency depends on configuration and failures, but the changed cost is once per already-existing warning and not part of subprocess launch synchronization.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Startup filesystem and subprocess costs are pre-existing and unchanged; attribution adds only bounded metadata.

Scenarios.Scenario: Extension progress in non-notification and notification locations without an audited ID
Scenarios.CriticalPath: All extension progress starts now destructure and forward notificationId, which is undefined for existing callers. Main-thread attribution performs one map-key construction and lookup before dispatching to the existing progress service. Notification updates continue through the existing throttled report path without repeating attribution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing progress start/report/end extension-host RPC sequence
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One start and end per operation, with existing reports throttled to at most one per 100 ms; the diff adds no call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical RPC cardinality with generic extension progress attribution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Progress task execution is not made to await the start RPC; report/end behavior is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-time attribution operation per progress operation, independent of report count, task duration, or collection size. Static allowlist arrays contain at most eight entries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing per-operation start/report/end RPCs and progress-service concurrency are unchanged. There is no shared burst, fan-out, or extra work per update.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A static map is available from module initialization; undefined IDs take the generic fallback immediately after one bounded map lookup. Cold and warm behavior differ only by ordinary module initialization already required for notification telemetry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the exact start and report paths show that notificationId is handled only at start.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extensions may create many progress operations, but changed work scales with operation starts, not updates, and remains bounded by tiny static collections.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The small per-start allocation/lookup does not establish meaningful CPU, GC, IPC, or rendering degradation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 31 changed files and every diff page. Traced message and progress metadata through proposal validation, IPC, bounded allowlisting, notification creation, rendering telemetry, OAuth network flows, Git filesystem checks, and TypeScript subprocess startup. No diff-introduced actionable performance regression was found, and the PR does not itself fix a proven shipped performance regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
